title: Information and Incentives
tagline: Adverse selection, signalling, screening, moral hazard and principal–agent contracts, incentives in organisations, incomplete contracts, mechanism design and efficient mechanisms
summary: When one side of a transaction knows more than the other, markets and organisations have to be designed around the information gap. This course develops the economics of asymmetric information: adverse selection and market unravelling, signalling and screening, moral hazard and the design of incentive contracts, incentives in organisations and incomplete contracts, and mechanism design with the revelation principle — with applications to insurance, credit, labour markets and regulation.

chapters.title: Asymmetric information and adverse selection
chapters.summary: Akerlof’s market for lemons, market unravelling, and adverse selection in insurance and credit.

chapters.title: Signalling in markets
chapters.summary: Spence’s model of job-market signalling, separating and pooling equilibria, and the intuitive criterion.

chapters.title: Screening and self-selection
chapters.summary: The Rothschild–Stiglitz insurance model and nonlinear pricing when buyers’ types are hidden.

chapters.title: Moral hazard and the principal–agent problem
chapters.summary: Hidden actions, the trade-off between risk sharing and incentives, and optimal contracts.

chapters.title: Incentives in organisations
chapters.summary: Multitasking, career concerns, tournaments and relational contracts.

chapters.title: Incomplete contracts and the boundaries of the firm
chapters.summary: The hold-up problem, property rights and the theory of the firm.

chapters.title: Mechanism design and the revelation principle
chapters.summary: Social choice functions, incentive compatibility, the revelation principle and the Gibbard–Satterthwaite theorem.

chapters.title: Efficient mechanisms and public decisions
chapters.summary: Vickrey–Clarke–Groves mechanisms, budget balance and the Myerson–Satterthwaite impossibility theorem.
